sections.content:
You know *por eso* from A2 Unit 5 and *así que* from B1 Unit 1. B1 Unit 16 added *como consecuencia*, and B1 Unit 32 added *como resultado* and *por esa razón*. All of them say that something follows from what you have just said. This lesson adds three more formal markers and puts them all on one scale, from everyday to formal.

• *así que*: "so". The everyday one, in speech and in writing.
• *de modo que*: "so", "which means that". It joins the fact and its result in one sentence.
• *por lo tanto*: "therefore". It usually starts a new clause, after a full stop or a semicolon, and a comma follows it.
• *por consiguiente*: "consequently". The same job, a little more formal.
• *en consecuencia*: "as a result", "accordingly". The same job again, common in reports and notices.

All of them state a result that is true, so the verb after them is in the indicative. *Por lo tanto*, *por consiguiente* and *en consecuencia* can also sit in the middle of the second clause, between commas.

sections.title: From everyday to formal
rows: Tenía mucho trabajo, así que se quedó en la oficina.
He had a lot of work, so he stayed at the office.
No había nadie en casa, de modo que dejé una nota.
There was nobody at home, so I left a note.
La lluvia fue muy fuerte; por lo tanto, cancelaron el partido.
The rain was very heavy; therefore, they cancelled the match.
El museo estaba cerrado; por consiguiente, no pudimos entrar.
The museum was closed; consequently, we could not go in.
Las ventas bajaron; en consecuencia, la empresa cerrará una oficina.
Sales fell; as a result, the company will close an office.

sections.content: *Porque* gives the reason and *por lo tanto* gives the result, so they point in opposite directions: *Cancelaron el partido porque llovía* but *Llovía; por lo tanto, cancelaron el partido*. After *de modo que* the subjunctive would give a purpose, "so that", like *para que* (B1 Unit 4). Here the result is real, so the indicative is used.
